author: Falsiq
quote: I've played around 29 hours of GTA VI so far, and I genuinely don't understand how people are calling this a masterpiece. My biggest problem is that it barely feels like GTA anymore. It feels like Rockstar took Red Dead Redemption 2, threw some cars and modern buildings into it, and called it GTA VI. Everything is slower, more restrictive, and way more focused on realism than actually being fun. The first 10 hours are **** exhausting. The pacing is terrible, the missions are repetitive, and the game constantly forces you to do boring **** before letting you experience anything interesting. It honestly feels like a life simulator at times, and no, making everything realistic doesn't automatically make it good gameplay. Then there's the freedom, or the lack of it. What happened to just jumping into GTA and doing whatever the hell you wanted? Now you've got a karma system, activities and interactions locked behind progression, NPCs reacting to your behavior, and ridiculously overpowered cops that make causing chaos more frustrating than entertaining. I understand what Rockstar was trying to achieve, but I don't understand why anyone would pretend this offers the same experience as previous GTA games. It doesn't. The whole game feels like it's constantly telling you how to play. The missions aren't much better either. Sure, there are some genuinely great moments, and a few missions are absolutely fantastic. But those are exceptions. Most of the time, you're following instructions, watching conversations, driving somewhere, and repeating the same boring routine. Having a massive open world means very little when the actual gameplay feels so restrictive. And the worst part? The game is technically incredible. The graphics, animations, NPC behavior, world details, all of that is impressive. I won't deny it. But I really couldn't care less about how realistic an NPC's daily routine is when I'm bored out of my mind playing the game. I'm also tired of this idea that criticizing GTA VI means you don't appreciate good games. I can appreciate the insane amount of work that went into it while still thinking the actual experience is disappointing. Maybe people who love Red Dead Redemption 2 and slow, heavily scripted experiences will absolutely love this game. That's fine. But I wanted GTA, not a crime-themed life simulator where I have to worry about consequences every time I want to have some fun. After 29 hours, I can say it's not a terrible game. It's just a massive disappointment compared to what I expected from GTA. Rockstar created one of the most detailed open worlds I've ever seen, but somehow made me feel less free than I did playing GTA San Andreas over 20 years ago. And for a GTA game, that's a pretty **** big problem.
